walkthroughs.body_html:
Chemistry of the Environment — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Chemistry of the Environment brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Chemistry of the Environment.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: The entropy of the surroundings must stay constant for the process to be spontaneous.
It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.
A catalyst lowers the activation energy of the original reaction pathway.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.

mcqs.q: For a process to be spontaneous, what must happen to the total entropy of the universe?
options: Reduction means a substance becomes physically smaller in size.
The entropy of the system must increase for the process to be spontaneous.
It must increase (ΔS_total > 0) — the system's entropy alone can decrease as long as the surroundings' entropy increases more.
The entropy of the surroundings must stay constant for the process to be spontaneous.

mcqs.q: What is reduction in terms of electrons?
options: Reduction means losing oxygen and oxidation means gaining oxygen — full stop.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
Gain of electrons (the oxidation number is reduced).
Reduction means a substance becomes physically smaller in size.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Crude oil”?
options: Methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆, propane C₃H₈, butane C₄H₁₀.
Mixture of hydrocarbons (mostly alkanes), separated by fractional distillation.
Contains only single C–C bonds; cannot add more atoms across a bond.
Saturated hydrocarbon with general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ — all single bonds.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Combustion of alkanes”?
options: Methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆, propane C₃H₈, butane C₄H₁₀.
Complete: alkane + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O. Incomplete: produces CO and soot.
Contains only single C–C bonds; cannot add more atoms across a bond.
Compound containing only hydrogen and carbon.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Alkane”?
options: Mixture of hydrocarbons (mostly alkanes), separated by fractional distillation.
Complete: alkane + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O. Incomplete: produces CO and soot.
Saturated hydrocarbon with general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ — all single bonds.
Methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆, propane C₃H₈, butane C₄H₁₀.

options: Mixture of hydrocarbons (mostly alkanes), separated by fractional distillation.

Compound containing only hydrogen and carbon.
